newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC expects to cover Korea unit debt - TV.
newsitem.headline: IPC expects to cover Korea unit debt - TV.

text.p: Computer company IPC Corp said it should be able to cover its estimated exposure of Singapore $45.5 million to its troubled Korean subsidiary in full, state television reported. But the company added that after doing so, it does not expect profits for the 1996 financial year to be positive.
IPC's South Korean subsidiary, IPC Corporation (Korea) Ltd (IPCK) defaulted on repaying 570 billion won worth of promissory notes on Wednesday.
IPC shares were suspended in Singapore on Thursday, having last traded at S$0.56.

On Friday, IPC informed the Singapore Stock Exchange it estimated its Korean exposure at S$45.5 million. IPC added it had not been able to contact or locate the chief executive officer of IPCK and that it was investigating the matter.
State television said that the company expected trading of its shares to resume in Singapore on Monday.
